paper.title: Algorithm 840: Computation of grid points, quadrature weights and derivatives for spectral element methods using prolate spheroidal wave functions, prolate elements
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 31(1) (TOMS 840, March 2005), 149-165
paper.note: DOI not verified in this wake; the article was not read (ACM Digital Library), so the claim rests on the shipped reference output.

code.archive: sha256 b213f74e8eadba736256700f462906138d71615c29fefdbb871b5a3ba5703aff (netlib.org/toms/840.gz as fetched 2026-11-26, HTTP 200, 829 lines, one shell archive created 2005-05-12)
code.note: MATLAB. Extract with /bin/sh after stripping the lines above '#! /bin/sh' (the archive header says so). Members: Matlab/Dp/Drivers/Res (reference output), TP_Lobptsts_MAIN.m (driver: prompts for N and c with input(), so feed N=6 and c=5 on stdin), TP_LobptswtsPERT.m, and Src/ (PN_Legendre_vectN.m, PNx_, PNxx_, TP_LobattoQuad.m, TP_Lobattoresid.m, TP_NewtonJAC.m, TP_eigprolODE.m).

field: numerics (spectral element grids and quadrature with prolate spheroidal functions)

claim.location: The shipped reference output Matlab/Dp/Drivers/Res, header 'Reference solution: N=6, c=5': xprol(2) = -0.7456 and wprol(3) = 0.5305 (the first vector printed, xprol = -1.0000 -0.7456 -0.2705 0.2705 0.7456 1.0000 and wprol = 0.0756 0.3939 0.5305 0.5305 0.3939 0.0756). The driver's own run, with N=6 and c=5, is what the file records.
claim.metric: Grid point xprol(2) and quadrature weight wprol(3) for N=6, c=5 printed by the reference run, compared as absolute differences.
claim.paper_value: Not used: the TOMS article was not read in this wake; the values are taken from the shipped reference output.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The shipped output prints four decimals, so its own rounding is up to 5e-5. 2e-4 is four times that rounding and far below the grid spacing (about 0.27 between xprol(2) and xprol(3)), so a wrong grid or weight would fail it. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 2 minutes: one Octave or MATLAB run with N=6, c=5.
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: A deterministic spectral-element quadrature code, whose shipped reference run prints grid points and weights for a small case; reproducing them exercises the prolate eigenproblem and Newton solve, in the MATLAB stack that most of the queue lacks.
